newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Commonwealth urged to press Nigeria on rights.
newsitem.headline: Commonwealth urged to press Nigeria on rights.

text.p: A British group that campaigns against media censorship urged the Commonwealth on Wednesday not to ease pressure on Nigeria, saying respect for human rights in the military-ruled African country had not improved.

"It would be a total betrayal if Commonwealth leaders decide to lift Nigeria's suspension," the acting director of Article 19 pressure group, Malcolm Smart, told a body set up by Commonwealth heads of state to monitor Nigeria.
Nigeria was suspended in 1995 from the group of Britain and its former colonies after it defied world opinion and hanged nine minority rights activists including author Ken Saro-Wiwa.
The Commonwealth Ministerial Action Group was set up afterwards to press Nigeria to restore democracy and respect individual liberties.

"Commonwealth leaders should not be fooled by Nigerian government promises to return the country to democratic rule when human rights continue to be so openly flouted," the London-based Article 19 said in a statement faxed to Lagos.
Military leaders are implementing a programme of transition to civilian rule they say will lead to a handover of power to a democratically elected president on October 1 next year.

Opponents dismiss the programme as a ruse to perpetuate military rule and point to continued detention of opposition figures including Moshood Abiola, presumed winner of an annulled 1993 presidential election.

Article 19 said the Commonwealth should not ease pressure on Nigeria in the runup to its summit in October when a decision would be taken whether or not to lift Nigeria's suspension or expel it from the group.
